components.text: JavaScript Async Programming and Promise Core Principles

In JavaScript runtimes like the browser and Node.js, asynchronous programming is core to handling I/O-intensive tasks. Traditional async relied on callback functions, leading to "callback hell." The introduction of Promise in ES6 changed this predicament.

components.title: Promise
components.definition: A Promise object represents the eventual completion (or failure) of an asynchronous operation and its resulting value. It has three states: pending (in progress), fulfilled (succeeded), and rejected (failed). Once the state changes, it will not change again.
components.example:
const promise = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
  setTimeout(() => {
    resolve('Success!');
  }, 1000);
});

promise.then((value) => {
  console.log(value); // "Success!"
});
